mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals an accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with declining FEDFUNDS, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 4.0% for two consecutive months, it indicates labor market weakness that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods with UNRATE > 4.0%, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and rise in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals housing sector contraction amid monetary tightening, reducing aggregate demand and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods with HOUST decline and FEDFUNDS rise, or interaction term Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansions, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals manufacturing sector weakness that reduces corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of late-cycle periods with INDPRO decline, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising retail sales growth (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer spending that boosts corporate revenues, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with rising RSAFS, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months, it signals restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and dampens economic activity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods with FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals labor market overheating without supply growth, leading to inflationary pressures and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods with PAYEMS rise and INDPRO fall, or interaction term Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high labor market tightness regimes, a decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% signals wage inflation risks that prompt central bank tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods during high labor market tightness with UNRATE < 3.5%, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.
